bugs.what: Distance/direction hints given in dialogue (e.g. 'three north of the head-frame, three east') often didn't match the actual room graph, making some sub-quest destinations (like the slag-hound's den in Cinderhall) hard to reach by dead reckoning.

Paginated action menus (p1/2, p2/2) sometimes shifted the numbering of a just-used action (e.g. 'use dried herbs' silently consumed the item on a page where I meant to pick a different numbered option), leading to an accidental item use.
bugs.where: The Kings' Rest — the Old Court, menu pagination

confusions: It was never fully clear whether resting a companion's personal grief-hold vs just doing the main hold's grief-rite were the same action or separate, until 'status' spelled it out — first-time players may under- or over-invest in companion quests without checking status.

The 'stands' unit of distance in NPC directions doesn't reliably equal one room-hop, so multi-step travel directions ('west five stands, then north twice') required trial-and-error rather than being followable literally.
suggestions: Let 'travel to a known place' surface named sub-locations (like a specific NPC's camp) once discovered, not just major landmarks, to cut down on manual backtracking.
Make directional hints from NPCs consistently equal to room-hops so players can navigate by dead reckoning without guesswork.
Show a small 'X hollows rested / needs' counter in the main HUD line (not just in status) since it's the primary win-condition tracker.
On paginated menus, keep a used-up action's number from being silently reassigned to a different action on the same keypress context.
